title: Residency constraints & benchmark scope - POC kickoff
summary: POC kickoff to define private networking approach and residency constraints for an inference POC. Customer requires EU-only data residency for model inputs/outputs and strict egress controls; evaluating VPC peering vs PrivateLink and on-prem option. Agreed success criteria (latency, throughput, cost targets), workload sizing, benchmarks, and a 6-week tentative timeline. Next: Redwood to share security docs, benchmark harness, and initial cost/config proposal; customer will share sample dataset footprint and expected concurrency profile.
topics: Benchmark targets: p95 latency, tokens/sec, concurrency
next_steps: Maya to send SOC2 + architecture whitepaper and Private deployment checklist by 2025-11-17
Liam to provision benchmark harness and sample load scripts and share endpoint by 2025-11-19
Cobalt to provide sample data shape, avg sequence length, and expected concurrency matrix by 2025-11-18
Schedule 2-hour bench run window week of 2025-11-24 (TBD)
action_items: Maya Chen; Send security package (SOC2, ISO summary, KMS notes); 2025-11-17
Liam Ortiz; Deliver benchmark harness + instructions; 2025-11-19
Tom Reyes; Provide VPC CIDR ranges, account IDs, and proxy egress rules; 2025-11-18
Priya Nair; Share compliance checklist and any legal redlines re: data residency; 2025-11-20
transcript:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll give it a quick agenda, scope the POC and then get into networking and benchmarks.
[00:12] Aisha Kapoor: Thanks Maya. We've got Tom and Priya here. Quick context: Cobalt is running ML inference for customer risk-scores, and we need to keep all customer data in EU regions, no cross-border egress. We're exploring Redwood for inference.
[00:29] Liam Ortiz: Awesome. Quick clarifier — when you say EU-only, do you mean control plane in EU too or just the data path for payloads?
[00:36] Aisha Kapoor: Prefer both, ideally. Control plane can be US if metadata is anonymized but payloads must never leave EU.
[00:44] Tom Reyes: And we have strict egress rules: only allowed outbound to our logging and metrics endpoints. No direct internet egress from the subnet used for inference.
[00:53] Maya Chen: Understood. Two common options we'll propose: VPC peering (low latency, cross-account peering) or PrivateLink/PrivateLink-like NAT-free endpoints. We also support on-prem private deployments if you need air-gapped.
[01:06] Priya Nair: Is PrivateLink fully supported for model serving? We need assurance that traffic never touches public routes.
[01:12] Liam Ortiz: Yes, PrivateLink creates an ENI in your VPC and uses AWS private network paths — in our tests it stays within AWS backbone. We do need to confirm region placement and account IDs. There's also the routing nuance: peering allows direct RFC1918 routes, PrivateLink uses NLB + ENI.
[01:27] Aisha Kapoor: What about egress for licensing checks or usage telemetry?
[01:31] Maya Chen: By default the hosted control plane may see metadata; for the POC we can do a Private deployment with a customer-managed control plane (or restricted telemetry) so tokens and payloads stay within your VPC and region. We'll share the Private deployment checklist.
[01:44] Evan Brooks: On benchmarks — our product target is p95 request latency < 200ms for 512-token sequences and throughput for 5 concurrent steady users but expect spikes to 80 concurrent during batch jobs.
[01:55] Liam Ortiz: Helpful. Can you give us typical tokens per second and avg sequence length?
[01:58] Aisha Kapoor: Avg sequence is 320 tokens; 95th is ~800. For tokens/sec during batch jobs we see bursty 2k-3k tokens/sec.
[02:09] Liam Ortiz: Great — for sizing we'll run baseline: single shard latency test, then concurrency ramp to 100 concurrent to simulate spikes. We'll instrument KV cache behavior — just a note, sometimes transcripts mis-say KV as K-V cache or "K-V cash" so ignore that — but the point is we can enable prefix caching to reduce cost/latency.
[02:26] Tom Reyes: We have a strict proxy egress pattern. Any outbound allowed must go through our egress proxy with TLS inspection. How does Redwood handle that?
[02:34] Maya Chen: For Private deployments you can configure egress through your NAT or proxy, and we support mTLS to your collector endpoints. For hosted we can configure PrivateLink so the data path never traverses internet, but some control callbacks may still leave region unless you opt-into dedicated control plane.
[02:50] Priya Nair: And KMS? We require customer-managed KMS with HSM.
[02:55] Liam Ortiz: We support integrating with customer KMS providers, and for Private deployments we can use your KMS for model keys and data-at-rest encryption. We'll include specifics in the security doc.
[03:04] Aisha Kapoor: Success criteria — beyond residency, we need p95 < 200ms at 50 concurrent, and 99% availability during test. Also cost per 1M tokens should be <= our internal threshold, we'll share the number.
[03:16] Maya Chen: Noted. For POC we usually propose: 1) functional residency test (payloads remain in EU) 2) perf benchmark: latency and throughput at target concurrency 3) reliability: no failed requests under expected load 4) ops handover: runbook and config for production cutover.
[03:31] Evan Brooks: Timeline? We need this validated before our Q1 planning in mid-December.
[03:36] Maya Chen: We can run a 6-week POC: week 0-1 config & infra (VPC peering/PrivateLink set up), week 2 benchmark runs & tuning, week 3-4 extended soak and edge-cases, week 5 security signoff and runbook, week 6 final report and handoff. That would shave into early December.
[03:52] Aisha Kapoor: That sounds reasonable. Any blockers on Redwood side?
[03:55] Liam Ortiz: Access to your AWS account IDs, VPC CIDRs, and ability to create endpoints. Also sample payloads and expected concurrency matrix so we can pre-size.
[04:05] Tom Reyes: We'll provide the CIDRs and can create the endpoints, but we want Redwood to provide exact CloudFormation snippets or Terraform.
[04:12] Maya Chen: We'll provide Terraform + quick-start scripts. We'll also include a hardened config that restricts egress to your proxy endpoints.
[04:20] Priya Nair: Legal — any data-processing addendum? We need EU data processing terms and potential subprocessor list.
[04:27] Maya Chen: Yes we'll include the DPA and subprocessor list in the security packet. For the POC we can sign an addendum if required.
[04:35] Evan Brooks: One more: when you talk about dedicated control plane vs managed, what are tradeoffs?
[04:39] Liam Ortiz: Dedicated control plane gives you isolation and the control plane sits inside your VPC — lower telemetry but more ops on your side. Managed control plane is faster to stand up but metadata may cross regions unless configured. For strict residency we recommend dedicated or private deployment.
[04:54] Aisha Kapoor: Bench specifics — can you run tokenized RPS tests vs. synthetic examples? We have some tokenization quirks in our data.
[05:02] Liam Ortiz: Yes, we ask customers to provide a small sample of representative payloads. We'll tokenize them with the same tokenizer used in the model and run the bench with that. We'll also run cold-start/prefix-cache tests and warm-KV cache tests.
[05:16] Tom Reyes: For metrics/observability, do we get agent-level traces? We need per-token cost breakdowns and latency per-step.
[05:24] Maya Chen: Redwood Console exports token-level cost and latency breakdowns. We'll give you dashboard access for the POC and an export of the trace data.
[05:31] Aisha Kapoor: Security question — do you write logs to S3? Are logs encrypted with our KMS?
[05:36] Liam Ortiz: For Private deployments, logs can land in your S3 with your KMS. For hosted we can configure dedicated buckets per customer with SSE-KMS in the EU.
[05:45] Evan Brooks: For the test harness, will Redwood generate traffic that respects our egress proxy and rate-limiters?
[05:50] Liam Ortiz: Yes we'll run traffic from within your VPC or from a peered endpoint, so it follows your egress path. We'll also throttle to simulate burst patterns.
[06:00] Priya Nair: Any concerns about model weights leaving region for load optimization?
[06:04] Maya Chen: Model weights remain at the serving location. We can pin model slices to EU-backed nodes and configure model variant fallbacks only to EU-region variants. We'll document the fallback behavior in case of capacity failover.
[06:17] Aisha Kapoor: On cost — early estimate?
[06:20] Maya Chen: We'll produce a POC cost sheet after we get your concurrency and token-rate numbers. For the bench we can cap spend and report back.
[06:27] Tom Reyes: Ok, who is the owner on Redwood side for engineering contact?
[06:30] Maya Chen: Liam will be the SE lead. I'm the AE and the contract owner.
[06:34] Evan Brooks: Great. Let's recap next steps.
[06:37] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood sends security pack + Terraform, bench harness; Cobalt shares sample payloads, CIDRs, and proxy endpoints; schedule bench window week of 11/24.
[06:48] Aisha Kapoor: Works for us. We'll try to get the samples over by Monday.
[06:52] Tom Reyes: We'll also draft the list of allowed egress FQDNs for the proxy.
[06:56] Maya Chen: Perfect. Anything else?
[06:58] Priya Nair: Please include your SOC2 subservice org names — we need to map controls.
[07:05] Liam Ortiz: Will do.
[07:10] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with the artifacts.
[07:14] Evan Brooks: Thanks.
[07:15] [call ends]
